newsitem.title: UK: Triplex steps up fight for William Cook.
newsitem.headline: Triplex steps up fight for William Cook.

text.p: British engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc on Tuesday stepped up its two-month fight for steel castings specialist William Cook Plc with a higher and final offer valuing the company at 74.8 million pounds.

Triplex said the revised offer was worth 400.7p per share to William Cook shareholders, outstripping the previous offer of 309p per share which valued the Sheffield-based group at just under 58 million pounds.

The new bid, widely predicted by analysts, sent William Cook shares to a record high of 390p in early trade, up 15p on the day, although volumes remained modest. The shares have risen 150p since Triplex launched its bid in November.

Triplex said the increased offer was final and was based on 21 new Triplex shares and 3,740p in cash for every 20 William Cook shares. Triplex previously offered seven of its shares and 1,350p cash for every nine William Cook shares.
Graham Lockyer, Triplex group chief executive, said he was optimistic the new bid would meet with approval.
"We believe we have pitched the offer at the right level and that William Cook shareholders will see this as a golden opportunity," Lockyer said in a telephone interview.
Triplex said it believed the planned acquisition could generate at least 2.5 million pounds of additional operating profit annually because of incremental sales and cost savings.

Triplex said the similarities between the two companies' casting activities would enable Triplex to carry out a rapid integration on a low-risk basis. Lockyer called the complementary skills the key to the expected profit gain.

Triplex specialises in using sand, ceramics and chemicals to produce moulds and cores, smelting and pouring metals and assembling cast products. Overseas sales account for around 41 percent of total sales of 82 million pounds. William Cook manufactures steel castings and targets British markets.

"We will realise at least an additional 2.5 million annualised and by the second year we will be at that rate...it is quick because we are fundamentally casting companies and we deploy very similar processes and key skills," he said.
Lockyer said both companies had what he called a very small amount of overlap but he said there was opportunity to increase cross-selling between the two companies.
"We will get good growth at the underlying level and have growth potential from complementary markets," Lockyer said.

Under the terms of the new offer, William Cook shareholders would also be offered a fully underwritten cash alternative of 383.4 pence per share. Also a share election and loan note alternative would be offered, the company said.
